answer: A farm cannot buy its way up the queue: the registry forge casts one ferrous marble per heat, one heat per day on a shared timeline, and each identity holds its own heat's marble. No two identities share a heat, so slots are serial and money cannot mint extra days. An honest agent pays $45 once for casting and assay; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 distinct heats, 1,000 days of serial waiting. Verifiers assay a marble's tracer ratio and roll period against its heat entry; two identities checked in one window must each produce their own, and a re-forged or wrong-heat marble mismatches and earns zero.
